idiom_name: protoc-gen-go generated messages, or encoding/json struct tags plus a compiled JSON Schema validator
implementation_notes: Go makes the binding explicit through struct shape: with schema-first IDL, protoc-gen-go generates message structs whose unknown fields survive decoding and protojson maps them to the JSON rendering of the same published language; with JSON contracts, struct tags (`json:"order_id"`) define the wire names and a compiled schema (github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6: NewCompiler, AddResource, Compile, Validate) enforces the published document at the seam. Choose the IDL path when participants are polyglot and evolution must be strict; plain encoding/json suffices when the schema document is the only artifact. A hand-written marshaller survives only for legacy binary layouts.
pitfalls: encoding/json ignores unknown fields and leaves missing numbers at their zero value: 'absent' and 'zero' are indistinguishable unless fields are pointers, generics/optionals, or the payload is validated against the schema first.
Generated .pb.go files must be regenerated in lockstep with the .proto and the google.golang.org/protobuf runtime; a stale generated file compiles cleanly and speaks the old contract.
Decoding into map[string]any or interface{} turns numbers into float64 and loses large uint64 ids - decode into typed structs or use json.Decoder with UseNumber.
